text.p: The European Union has pledged to abolish all state monopolies over telecoms services and infrastructure in most countries by January 1, 1998.
That deadline will force governments to take the final liberalisation step by opening their lucrative voice telephone markets to competition.

The European Commission, arguing that a competitive telecoms market is essential for Europe's economic growth, has already used special treaty powers to issue a series of laws to pry open other sectors.

The EU executive ordered governments last January to introduce full competition in their mobile phone markets. It had earlier ordered them to allow cable TV networks by the start of 1996 to carry telecoms services such as data transmission that had already been opened to competition.

The Commission also said last year EU states must allow new telecoms operators to bypass state phone companies and use "alternative networks" such as those operated by utility companies to carry liberalised telecoms services by July 1, 1996.
EU rules allow Greece, Ireland, Luxembourg, Portugal and Spain to request delays in implementing some of the telecoms liberalisation deadlines because they have small or less developed networks.

In the process of clearing the Unisource telecoms joint venture involving Telefonica de Espana, the Commission negotiated a plan under which Spain would open up its markets to full competition by November 1998.
It has cleared a plan by Ireland to introduce full liberalisation by the start of 2000 and must rule on formal requests for delays from the other countries.
